utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The map on the overhead projector, Mr. Grebenar, although not the most detailed of maps nevertheless shows highlighted in red Poculica, and to remind the Judges, it lies on what is being called certainly by English military personnel the mountain road between Zenica and Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the English army called them. I think that we called them the regional road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Poculica is pretty nearly at the top of the mountain; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you call that a mountain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a large village in two parts, the upper section nearer Zenica being the Muslim section, and the lower section nearer Vitez being the Croat section; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, if you separate it into two sections. In my statement, I divide it into three sections, but two is also possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, just to give the or remind the Court of distances, although the hill or mountain on which this village sat operated as a division between Zenica and Vitez, the road between Zenica and Vitez would only take about 20 minutes to drive in ordinary circumstances; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were only about ten minutes by car away from the centre of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have very many questions to ask you, but I'll try and deal with them broadly speaking in chronological order. You speak of being in the position of a guard and asked to take some commanding role by a meeting of people in your village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is correct that I was proposed then or rather nominated for making up these lists for the guard and to see everybody, and to see who the volunteers would be for this guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've heard about decrees of -- for the armed forces that were made in July and October of 1992. In 1992, you were, of course, of military age. Did you not have a fully identified military role in your area by the autumn of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying, are you, that the formation of a guard in your village was an entirely independent activity of the villagers although you were only ten minutes away from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wonder if you could just look, please, at document 1410.1. There's about three new documents and this is one of them and that's all. When do you say the guards were established, Mr. Grebenar? When were they established, the guards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think sometime around the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at this document, please, this is a document and it's dated 1994. If we can lay it on top of the map, because I'll be returning to the map, thank you very much. It's dated 1994, and it certifies that you, I think, born in 1960, were wounded and had been a member of the Vitez Brigade since the 8th of April 1992. The certificate is issued for the purpose of establishing the status of disabled war veteran and not for any other purpose. It's signed Dzuric. Now, can you explain that document to us, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can. This is a document that belongs to me. I got it in order to exercise my rights of a war veteran who is disabled. This date, the 8th of April, 1992, I said that the village guards were established sometime around the beginning of 1992. When this document was being issued, they put that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I'm going to suggest to you is that far from there being an independent business of the guards, what was happening in your village was quite integrated with what was going on elsewhere, and that's reflected by the fact that you identified yourself as a member of the Vitez Brigade in April of 1992. Because you did regard yourself as part of the Vitez Brigade doing whatever work you were doing for the HVO in your village, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand whether this was a question or whether this was a comment of yours. No, I did not consider myself to be a member of the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Why does the document say "a member of the Vitez Brigade" if you weren't?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, of course I'm asking you. Now reply.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I was wounded as a member of the Vitez Brigade, that is to say, that if mobilisation was on the 16th, I was wounded and then when I asked for a certificate in order to exercise my rights on the basis of the fact I was wounded, they wrote that I was a member of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't understand. Were you a member of the Vitez Brigade or not? It's a perfectly plain question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member of the Vitez Brigade, I was that from the 16th onwards but since I was wounded on the 16th, I was not an active member. When, after my sick leave, when I was wounded, when I reported back at the front line, I considered myself to be a member of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, the document says he's a member since the 8th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And we can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, you said that you considered yourself a member of the brigade as from the 16th of April of 1993 but you went through no formalities of joining up that brigade, did you, on the 16th of April? There was no recording of the fact that you now regarded yourself as a member of the brigade as of that date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that if we look at a document that -- if I hand this in, it will save time. It's an existing exhibit, it's number 808, it's a list of names with an English translation of what it amounts to. So if we can lay the English translation on the ELMO and then follow it with the list where we've reminded ourselves of the content of the document. So if you just put the English page on the first, please, thank you very much. What we're looking at here, and I'm going to read the English summary, is a document from the Viteska Brigade dated eight days after you decided yourself that you were a member of the brigade, that is the 24th of April, a list of the Viteska Brigade soldiers killed in the conflict with Muslim forces. And if we then turn to the next page please, we see that on this document, your name is listed on the first of the two sheets I think you'll find it there. Thank you very much. And we can see that your name is listed on that date, thank you very much, "Dragan Grebenar," you see? Now, how are you being listed as soon as the 24th of April of 1993 before any question of getting a pension arises and right in the middle of the conflict, how are you being listed then as a member of the Viteska Brigade, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know how to answer this. I said -- well, I mean if there was general mobilisation on the 16th, and I regard myself as one from the 16th. That was my understanding at least, that on the 16th there was a general mobilisation, and then I became a member of the Vitez Brigade. That was the 16th of April of 1993 and this is the 24th of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've made the point. There is another document to the like effect. If I give the Chamber the number of the document, I needn't place it before the witness. It's 957.1 and that's a document in May of 1993. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just complete this exercise and then I'll be done with documents, I think, and I only have a few more questions to ask. May we look, please, at 1477.10, please. . Now, this document that you're looking at is a certificate. Now, this is dated the 9th of March of 1998, much later. It's signed by a military person, Brigadier Vinac, and it confirms that you, born in 1960, from Dobrovica, were a member of the brigade in the period the 8th of April to the 19th of January, 1996, and what's more, that you performed the duties of a platoon commander. Now, if your guards in your village were an informal arrangement, why are you being given the formal title of platoon commander, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a certificate that I also needed, in terms of the circumstances involved, I mean, in terms of the duties that I was discharging when I was wounded. This is from 1998; you can see that. So how should I put this, an attempt was made to help me in order to promote me so that when my disability was to be assessed, I could have greater financial compensation. So that was the reason why this was written the way it's been written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that this is a dishonest document where it says you were platoon commander because you were no such thing; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the truth that the HVO's activities in the area just ten minutes from Vitez were, indeed, coordinated and that you were in charge as a platoon commander of what was going on in your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as military matters are concerned, I was not involved in any duties, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then finally, 1472.10 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. Finally, 1472.10, this is an earlier document. I should have perhaps put them in the reverse order. The 24th of January, 1996. This is a certificate reflecting the circumstances of your being injured on the 16th of April in Poculica in the right shoulder blade and head, and it sets out, "... during an attack by ... Muslim Defence Forces ... wounded in the back ..." and then it says, "... while performing military duties on the first line of defence." You'll see that those words have been underlined, or they have been counted as underlined in the translation. But still, "performing military duties on the first line of defence," do you accept that, please, as a description of what you were doing on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I accept that, that on the 16th, during the attack, I was discharging a military duty and that I was involved in the defence of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The position of the Vitez Brigade in 1992 was, although you didn't tell us about this yesterday, that there was an active component of that brigade; correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Believe me, I'm not very knowledgable in these military matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you gave evidence in the case of Kupreskic, and you certainly there knew about it because you spoke of men who regarded themselves as sufficiently active or professional as soldiers, that they wouldn't be involved in mere village guard activities. Do you remember giving that evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can repeat now what I said then. But I did not understand your previous question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. My fault entirely. I'll go back to the question. There was an active component of the Vitez Brigade in 1992 distinguishable, even on your own account, from village guards; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've already seen, and therefore I don't need to trouble the Judges with it unless you want to see it, we've seen a document, 653 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Apparently there's been a revised translation at the request of me, so it ought to go in again just to be looked at very quickly. 653. Thank you. Yes. I'm grateful to Ms. Verhaag for reminding me that I was concerned about the original translation of the title of this document, and I've had it reconsidered. Your Honours may remember that I was concerned about this document which featured in the judgement of one of the other cases, from where under the title I think it referred to "List of Personnel Positioned," but we now see that the title of the document in English reads: "List of Personnel (Their Number) From the First Battalion Per Village of" and then "/? Deployment or Origin."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, Mr. Grebenar, the simple point is here, this is a document of the 14th of April of 1993 relating to the 1st Battalion of Vitez. Do you accept that that would be the active battalion of the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that, really, I'm not very knowledgable as far as these military terms are concerned. I don't know. I mean, this is the first time I've seen this document and I really can't comment on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What it's suggesting is that in the 1st Company or the 1st Battalion of the Viteska Brigade, there were some 13 soldiers in Poculica, or with deployment or origin in Poculica. Does that fit with your memory, that there would have been some 13 soldiers in Poculica who would have regarded themselves, in accordance with in your Kupreskic evidence, as sufficiently active or professional that they shouldn't be involved in activities in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From Poculica, there were some active volunteers, so to speak, who were active. I mean, when they were free, when they were off, it was up to them to decide whether they would join the village guards or not. But I think it was a smaller number. I can't really comment on that. This number, 13, I think it's too big.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move straight away to the night of the 15th/16th, I think. You've told us that you first got warning of what was coming at what time in the morning? What time did you tell us it was that you first heard of things, on the morning of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around 4.30 in the morning when I was awakened by these two men who were on guard that morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that these two men had been spoken to by a woman who had been spoken to by her sister. You haven't given us the name of the woman in this case, but I think in Kupreskic you said her name was Mara Papic. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, this is Mara Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Kupreskic, you said that this happened at 5.00, or possibly ten minutes before. That's not a huge difference. But was it half past four, an advanced time, or 5.00, do you think?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most correct thing to say would be that it was sometime in between, you see. I mean, it's been such a long time --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and I was awakened in the morning. I think it was between the two. It could not have been 5.00, but it was after 4.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last question on this. What was the source of information or intelligence about this forthcoming attack that the men told you the women had told them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the source of the information? Where do you say that information had originally come from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I do not understand the question. Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Where did you understand that the women had got the information that there was going to be an attack on your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Mara Papic received this information from her sister. But where she got this information from, from this other village, the neighbouring village, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No question of UNPROFOR or SFOR or whatever you think they were called providing that information, was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea, believe me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, you certainly gave no account of SFOR or UNPROFOR being the source of information in Kupreskic. But yesterday you told us, and it's at -- I'm afraid I don't have the page reference -- you said yesterday, unless the transcript's wrong, that there were SFOR stories that there would be an attack. Now, are you seeking to tell us that SFOR was the source of this information or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was either misunderstood or misinterpreted yesterday. I did not mention at all that this information could have come from SFOR or rather UNPROFOR at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whatever the cause of your getting up, presuming that you did get up early in the way you describe, if we go back to the map, please, if the usher would be good enough to take the document off, the position is, geographically, that from the high ground of Poculica you can see across to the villages of Ahmici and Santici, can you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only in part. Not in whole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once the attack on those villages began at half past five, those attacks were visible to you and indeed to any others in the village even if they were in another part of the village in the Muslim part of the village; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. At half past five, you couldn't see it. In the morning, we only heard gunfire and at first, it seemed to us that it was coming from the direction of Vitez and more to the right. And later on, however, we realised it was also coming from the direction of Ahmici and those areas. But it's not all that -- it's not that it's in full view. You can see a couple of houses in Ahmici, but only from the uppermost part of Poculica, that is the purely Muslim part of the village. From the lower part, you can only see two or three houses of Gorni, Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The point I want to make is this: The first time that there was any attack on your evidence on Poculica by ABiH forces was much later in the morning at what, half past 9.00 or 10.00?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shells began, I mean, around 8.00 or half past 8.00 and the sporadic gunfire started around 10.00 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, one way or another, any attack on the Croat part of the your village occurred a significant time after the attacks had begun on Ahmici and other places in the area generally; correct? A couple of hours, three hours, something like that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your village being a mere ten minutes by road from Zenica, you are quite unable to help us one way or another with whether any attack on your part of the village was simply a reaction by Muslim forces from Zenica to what they had then discovered of the attack on Muslim targets such as Ahmici and elsewhere; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that whether it was a reaction or not. I know that in the morning, at 8.00, the shelling began. Why were we attacked, whether it was a reaction or a purposeful attack, I cannot comment on that, but Poculica is more than 20 minutes away from Zenica rather than 10 minutes by car, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was advanced on behalf of Mr. Cerkez at one stage in this trial, it's page 8301 in the cross-examination by Mr. Kovacic of the witness Morsink, it was advanced that Poculica was a village that was, at one stage, surrounded by Croats. Now, we know that Poculica may be regarded as being in two sectors or three, but can be regarded as Muslim and Croat. Do you agree with that description that so far as the Muslim sector of the village was concerned that it was, at one stage, surrounded by Croats and attacked by them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, out of the question. I think you slipped when you said that the village was surrounded by Croats. The village could not be surrounded by Croats at any time. Since that from four sides, from Dubravica, from Sljivcica, they had a strategic point on Sljivcica towards Vitez, and then from the direction of Vjetrenice, Tolovici, to the right Vrhovine, we were surrounded, the Croats, were surrounded by Muslims that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the Muslim part of the village was at no stage under attack whether surrounded or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot claim as far as we, the villagers, are concerned. There was no attack, there could be no attack nor could there be an attack. There could be some sporadic gunfire during our retreat when we were withdrawing from the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we've also heard evidence -- I'm just checking on whether this witness was open or not, my recollection -- yes, from the man Breljas. This evidence, Mr. Grebenar, could be of either of 15th or 16th of April of 1993, but almost certainly relates to the 16th. And he speaks of grenades being discharged in the area of the mosque. Now, the mosque is, of course, in the Muslim area of the village. Do you remember grenades being aimed at that mosque, page 11.757.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't recall that because I never managed to make it to the upper part of the village that day, not once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke in Kupreskic of a messenger, a Muslim messenger, coming to that part of the village. I don't think you've told us about that part in your evidence yesterday. Do you still say that happened or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention that. But it wasn't a Muslim courier, it was a young man who was in the central part of the village who was our neighbour, a Muslim, and that morning, he started up there with a rifle and we told him, "Come on, just let the rifle be. Don't go there," because he would be firing at us. And later on, he came back when he saw all the things that were going on. When he saw, as he said, around the mosque there were lots of troops that he did not know and that they had already captured many and taken away and that everything was ready, and I claimed that that is how it was. But he came, I understood, he also returned of his own will because he must have been told by those that he should go back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about of this because of it's essential, it may be thought, improbability for a Muslim to come in these circumstances. Can you give us his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. I still do not know his name but I know the young man. His father is Asim Krehic and I think that the boy's name was Ahmed or -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I'm not sure his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two last questions, both about how you landed up in Kratine. Perhaps we can focus on that. It is visible on the screen at present. It's now well visible, thank you very much. Kratine is just, of course, just to the north or north-east of Ahmici and Nadioci; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is, although I'm not quite sure about the sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few hundred metres, a kilometre at the most, a couple of kilometres at the most from those villages; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to say, but I think it's more than Ahmici that Kratine is -- could be as many as three kilometres, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man Bralo was there, wasn't he, when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why down there in that village, there were people called Bralo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember a famous man called Bralo probably given rather elevated status by Croats, accorded respect; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- I may have heard about that Bralo later, much later. Late 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That Bralo was there with you, wasn't he, when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prisoners from there were taken, Muslim prisoners from there were taken trench digging, correct, against their will?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up there, while I was at the front line when I came, that is, no Muslims were brought to dig trenches. I had made a dugout for myself and that is where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last question is this: You say to the Judges that there was no firing on civilian targets while you were in Kratine. If we look at the map, all of the civilian targets within range of Kratine had already been cleansed of all Muslims, hadn't they? There were no targets left to fire on; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. I, from Kratine, I did not have any Muslim targets and besides, they were not within my range.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, perhaps you could help us with this: The map shows Kratine quite plainly. We've heard a lot of evidence about Kuber. Kuber, I think, does not appear on the map, but my recollection is that it's in that area. I don't know if the witness can help us with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my experience is this witness is really not good in geographical positionings. I, myself, gave up to ask him to show as he stated. But Kuber is visible, and you correctly said just a little bit right from Kratine but the letters are rather stretched over the mountain. That is why you can hardly find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is it -- it's on the plan, is it, that we have on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The K is under -- you can see it there, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry say that again, the K is under --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you look at the place called --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Go and point it out, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The witness is just showing that he can show.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness show. Would you like to show us, Mr. Grebenar, on the map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So that would be above Kratine, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Maybe it would be good just to finish that part since it was mentioned. Re-examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Grebenar, since we are on the subject of Kuber and Kratine, when did you come to that position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was sometime in mid-August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The front line was already stabilised there and there were only slight shifts. But at that time, was there any active combat at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The front lines were already there established, dug in, entrenched, and I think it moved back twice when I came there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And as my learned friend had mentioned that one, Bralo, and he was asking you questions about him so I have a couple of questions. Is Bralo a frequent surname in in that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the village of Nadioci there were quite a number of Bralos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have all the positions that you held here at Kratine ever met -- did you ever meet somebody name Cicko Bralo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw him up there on the positions on the ground at the time when I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But let us go back. Mr. Grebenar, do you know when the mobilisation was announced for all conscripts in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trust me, I never heard about it officially from any authorities, but it was said that it was the beginning of the attack, that is, the 16th of April. That is when we were attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if that was on the -- if it was indeed on the 16th of April, did anyone come to you to give you a document, a summons, or to tell you where as of today, you are a member of such and such unit and consider yourself mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 16th of April in the morning, did you feel as a member of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did your -- what was your affiliation with the village guards, and the first time under the circumstances, when did you see -- perceive yourself as a member of the brigade for the first time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to the front line at Kratine in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you arrived at the front line, did somebody tell you, well, so and so is your commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that commander, did he treat you as his soldier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, you received orders from him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, you were shown a document and there was mention of some 13 men. You said that there were less. But, right, there were a certain number of men who were members of the brigade. Would you please tell us, on the 16th of April, in the morning, in Poculica, did you see, apart from your village guards, any HVO units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any one of those 13 or dozen or ten men that you knew had been active in the brigade before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were all with us in the village together that morning, and I even tried to consult them as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they act differently from you at that time? Did they have any task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Grebenar, do you have any idea, do you know, did the Vitez Brigade exist in 1992? Do you think that would be a correct assumption?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not look like that to me. There were no indications, no signs of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know if in 1992 there was something called the 92nd Regiment, the so-called 92nd Vitez Regiment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard about the 92nd Home Guards Regiment in 1992/1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I heard about it in 1993, during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1994?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was still its name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As you were on sick-leave on those critical days, that is, on the 16th of April and then for the next few days, did you have an opportunity to discuss with your fellow guards in the village when it was that they were mobilised and eventually became members of the Vitez Brigade? Did you ever learn that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, believe me, we never talked about it. We simply did not think it important whether I was mobilised or not. When we were attacked, I simply thought it was my duty to defend myself. Whether I was mobilised, whether somebody would write that down, I did not care about it then, nor do I care about it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. When the war ended, in 1994/1995 and later, the question of some property rights was raised having to do with the woundings and one's service in the army, one's military service. Tell us, if a certain Dragan Vinac was ever your superior in any manner of speaking and in any way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a wounded member of the village guards, you wanted to exercise some of your property rights in that regard, that is, to get a disability benefit.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were various municipal proceedings that were started then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way did you have to prove that the wounding happened when one was on duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One had to get the various papers. Well, you know, the red tape. You needed some witnesses who had seen you be wounded, the circumstances of the wounding, and things like that. I was told then that I had to get those papers from that regiment - that was already in 1995, 1996 perhaps - that that was where I should go for that paper. And if I could get this document that I had been wounded on the front line -- well, one had to go through that procedure to get those papers about the circumstances of the wounding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You men who took part in those proceedings talked about it, because it took months, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that period of time of those proceedings, did you learn during the proceedings that members of village guards had been assigned a membership as of the 8th of April, 1994; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw on the certificate that I was issued that the date was the 8th of April, but I'm really not -- I don't know if everybody had certificates with that same date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told that the membership in village guards was being accorded that particular treatment as of that date and then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I was told when I was issued a certificate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the clerks who were responsible for the proceedings told you that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This document, 808, we don't have to go back to it, but it was signed by Zvonimir Cilic, if you remember, where it lists the men of the village, 92, 82, and the like -- no, sorry, I got it mixed up, where you are mentioned as a wounded person. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever tell you or report to anyone or let anybody know that you had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, my fault. I wasn't specific. When you were wounded, on that same day, or the next day when you were in hospital, did any one of your fellow village guards tell you that he'd let the authorities know that you had been wounded, that he had notified the authorities so that it would be put on record?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not tell me that but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I think I don't have any further questions, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Grebenar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, your next witness, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Our next witness is Mr. Zdenko Rajic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, if you'd like to take a seat. Yes, we've got our summaries. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The booths have not been given the summaries, if that can be distributed, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's coming around. Examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On behalf of the Defence of Mr. Cerkez, I'm going to ask you several questions regarding your testimony and I'm going to try to ask you to answer them to the best of your recollection. I would also like to ask you to please wait a bit after I ask you a question so that we give the interpreters an opportunity to fully interpret our exchange. Will you please state for the record your full name, date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: My name is Zdenko Rajic. I was born on 7 April 1969 in Rijeka, in Vitez municipality, where I reside to date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the village of Rijeka. This is a village which over time had become a part of the town of Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you are married. You have two children; your children's ages are two and a half and five.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a police officer by profession.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you also have a carpenter's trade.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You work for the Vitez Police Department currently.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, you had worked in the Brist company.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you became unemployed after that stint with the Brist factory in Zenica. Was that a common occurrence, that people would lose jobs in that period?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that this was happening across the board, in other words, to people of all ethnic backgrounds?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the war had first broken out in Slovenia, then Croatia, then it came to Bosnia-Herzegovina, you then volunteered to go and join the other soldiers who were at the defence line against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, where did you go to report as a volunteer?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I went to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to these defence lines and you were on the front lines at Galica, Potkraj, Skulja, Slatka Vode, Strikanice, Jajce, Bugojno, and the Mount Vlasic plateau. Are these all the locations where you were manning the defence lines together with other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in these shifts which you took, were you there as a member of the HVO, or were members of Muslim ethnic background also part of those units, first the TO and then the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was established in late 1992, you became its member; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later, after the Vitez Brigade was established, you became a member of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that you were first a member of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade and then the Vitez Brigade, you continued to go to all these locations to fight the JNA aggression.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. These shifts consisted of about 30 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I would like to take you back to the events in 1992. You just mentioned that you went to the defence lines in shifts of 30. How did that work? How was that done?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: These were groups of about 30 men. We stayed for about one week at the front line, and then on the way back, that is, after we were done, we were free for two or three weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, in 1992, this was all done on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you actually were a soldier while you were at the defence lines?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was only a soldier when I was at the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went back to your village, you went about your regular business which you conducted as a civilian.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in addition to your going with your shifts to the front line, you also had a duty to provide security for the command post of your battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that being a part of those shifts was a voluntary thing. Were there any means of coercion, that people were forced to go to the front lines?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. These were volunteers, and these were mostly people who had become unemployed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In late 1992 and the early part, the first four months of 1993, you went to the front line in those shifts, and that is how you spent that period of time.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, when was the last time that you went to Slatka Vode for a shift?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: That was around 20 March 1993. That was my last shift. And that did happen -- that happened to be Slatka Vode.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you went back to Rijeka, to Vitez, to your home.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came back, did you have a replacement at the front line?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, after the war, that is, the armed conflict, had broken out on 16 April 1993, that a shift from Vitez had remained surrounded at that location?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, let me point you now -- let me direct your attention to the events immediately preceding the events of the 16th of April. On 15th of April, were you on duty or were you off?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was off. I had the day off and I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, for you, was 15th April special in any way or was it just a regular day?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: To me, it was a regular day like any other day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, could you notice that anything unusual was happening and did you notice any grouping of military forces or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I could not. And as I said, I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you, in fact, become aware that something unusual was going on?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: That was in the morning of the 16th when I was awakened by explosions and small-arms fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from where did these explosions come and the small-arms fire?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: From all directions within the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After all these events, in conversations with your friends or acquaintances, had you heard that any kind of notice had come from the headquarters about a possible attack?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but only two or three days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on the -- in the night 15th to 16th, nobody told you anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you had heard those explosions early in the morning and after all that small-arms fire which had awakened you, what happened? Did you receive any call or anything?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: After I had woken up and having heard these explosions, I soon dressed and then the phone rang.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time could it have been?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Somewhere around 5.30, I don't know exactly but around that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The phone rang, I answered it, and it was my commander, Karlo Grabovac calling me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Karlo Grabovac was your superior. What military unit did he command?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he with the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: In 1993, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did Karlo Grabovac, your commander, tell you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He told me that I had to go to the Cvreno Brdce, that was the feature 517, and also if I saw any of my neighbours around, that I should tell them to head straight there because something was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give you any other orders?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He said that a new conflict had broken out in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the extend of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that your commander had directed you to the feature 517 which was also known as Crveno Brdce. Can you describe to us in which direction is this feature, around which village?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: That was in the direction of Vranjska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this feature strategically important with respect to the road Vranjska-Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. And also there were water reservoirs there, that is, that was drinking water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, in order to be able to see the Vranjska village, it is necessary to climb that feature, that -- to Crveno Brdce because Vranjska was in the valley below?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The road going to Vranjska, is it correct that this is the boundary line with the Busovaca municipality, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the lower part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you climbed up that hill from where you could see Vranjska in the morning of the 16th, did you observe anything, anything special, any -- did anything catch your attention in Vranjska?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Of course it did. The ABiH soldiers were being grouped there, and immediately we were shelled from all sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, after you reached the top of that feature, fire was opened on you from small-arms and also from artillery?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do? Did you return fire?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We took cover.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any trenches dug by that time?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was only after the attack that you started digging into -- to dig trenches and cover?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, Mr. Rajic, what was your military position?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was to protect the feature 517 because we had water reservoirs, it was palatable water there so we were to protect it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the attack was coming from the direction of the village of Vranjska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time, you were commander of the 1st Company third battalion of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you become that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: That was in May 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how you became the commander of the 1st Company, 3rd Battalion of the Vitez Brigade? Were you given any document? Who told you that you were now the commander?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not receive any documents, but somebody had to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander of the 3rd Battalion was Karlo Grabovac; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This 1st Company of yours, who were members of those 1st Company? Who was it composed of?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Those were the locals who had been village guards. So they were all inhabitants of the Rijeka village who had been involved in village watches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can say that the previously-established village guards were then incorporated into the Vitez Brigade and its 1st Company on the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you personally say as of what date did these village guards, these villagers, become incorporated and become the 1st Company of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: As of the date of the establishment of the Vitez Brigade, that is, from the start of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this company which, as you said, was composed of the members of the village guards, remained around the village of Rijeka to protect it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And throughout the war, it was never deployed anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, let me ask you this: You said later on you dug some trenches and fortified. Where were these trenches dug, on which ground?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The whole defensive lines were on Croat-held grounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You too have some property near your village, you have land?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is right above my house, about 100 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your property also used for the defence lines where the trenches were dug?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, 30 to 40 per cent of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And throughout the conflict, these trenches, these fortified lines were not moved?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, throughout this conflict, did you carry out any offensive operation? In other words, did you ever leave your trenches and move forward in the direction of the Vranjska village?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your basic goal was to defend your village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, tell us something about the village of Rijeka. Is this, in terms of ethnic composition, is it a mixed village or is it a mono-ethnic village?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was a mixed village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your village, Rijeka, also lived Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this attack or this conflict, were Muslim houses attacked by the locals?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict, did your Muslim neighbours continue to live in their homes?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were not involved, they were not engaged in the defence of the village as your Croat compatriots were; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a personal experience when you once helped a Muslim girl, can you tell us what it was?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This happened in late May early June, 1993. Soldiers who were at the front line saw a female who happened to find herself in the zone of -- in the combat zone. They had stopped her there and brought her over to me. And as I knew her, we were neighbours, her name is Hatidza Kajmak, she is from Kajmakovici. I escorted her through the minefield to the ABiH line and I released her there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did she, herself, express a desire to cross over that line and go in that direction?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you did that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and she is still alive today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, throughout this period when you were involved in the defence in your village in trenches, did you ever get any orders from your superiors or anyone else that you must take special care and that you have to treat Muslims in a special way? In other words, mistreat them, discriminate against them, to persecute them in any way?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We never received any such order to attack or persecute Muslims or any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of more comments about my client, Mr. Mario Cerkez. You know him from before, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your home is not far from Mr. Cerkez's home?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Those are -- we had neighborly relations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you -- what was Mr. Cerkez like? Was he an aggressive type of a person? Did he like to get into trouble?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, he was never aggressive. He was very communicative. He always wanted to assist people regardless of their ethnic background. He was never a nationalist. He was a good man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear him say anything belligerent or any -- in a hostile way against Muslim -- people of Muslim background?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I know Mario very well. He came several times to the front lines. He said first that we should protect the line. That we should protect lives. And he said that if we had an enemy soldier captured that he should be treated properly, in the military way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you follow those orders?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony you also mentioned -- you said that your fellow villagers in Rijeka who were Muslim stayed at home and were not involved in the military operations. Were they involved in any other activities such as digging fortifications or something else in your village?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, not with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the villagers, however, help you in digging fortifications during this conflict, however?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the elderly. These were Croat men and women of more advanced age.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajic, that will conclude my questions. Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That will be a convenient moment for a break. It is 11.00. We will adjourn now until half past 11.00. Mr. Rajic, would you remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence, please, until it's over, and that does include anybody from the Defence team. Could you be back, please, at half past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No questions from Mr. Kordic, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Somers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, so that we do not confuse you with a number of other Rajics, would you please tell us your father's name?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The late Franjo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You had two occupations as of 1991, both police officer and carpenter. Were you unable to find any particular work in either occupation at that time? Was there no industry that would have used your skills as a carpenter?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: In 1991, I did not have two professions. At that time I was a carpenter. As I already mentioned earlier on, I worked in Zenica in carpentry at Brist. And then at the end of 1991, I became jobless and became a policeman only in 1994, after I completed a course for policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies a point that was not clear. You have described the tasking of your military work in 1992 as essentially defensive, not offensive, against the Serb aggressor; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Only defence activities. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weaponry were you equipped with during 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I personally had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the type of weapon it was as an automatic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it, please? Was it a Kalashnikov, an Uzi? What type of weapon was it, please?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. The interpreter did not catch the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Repeat, please, for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Palovka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your venturing to places beyond the immediate area of your home, which was Rijeka, places like Jajce and ultimately Ahmici, was there a change in your mandate from simply guarding your home against Serb aggression to move to locations farther from home, such as Jajce and Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: My locations, as I already mentioned, were the entire Vlasic plateau, Jajce. As for Ahmici, could you please tell me the period when I was there? Could you please clarify that for me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The October 1992 incident at Ahmici, do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of October, 1992, yes, I do recall that, and I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get there? How did you become involved at that incident? What brought you to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was on duty between the 19th and 20th at the command post at Rijeka, in the house of Srecko Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn about the Ahmici incident so as to report there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: There was an incident. The main road was blocked, and also the Catholic cemetery at Topala. I heard about that from Goran Males, my colleague, and that was the night of the 19th. The BH army forces that had blocked the road and the Topolska cemetery were stopping and mistreating him, actually, and then they released him after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Males himself tell you this?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you actually get called to go to Ahmici? Was there a physical order issued; written, verbal? How did you know to go there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: There was a telephone call.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karlo Grabovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Karlo Grabovac was your commander, is that correct, at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well did you know Karlo Grabovac? Did you know him socially beside being under his command?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we knew each other before the conflict as well and we socialised, because he was a carpenter too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long before the conflict did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Five to eight to ten years, something like that. And we're not too far away either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as early as -- well, excuse me, let me ask you this: As at October 1992, he was your commander. When did he first become your commander during the year 1992? Was he at all times your commander, or when did he become your commander?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He was all the time while we were volunteers. And when we went to the JNA lines or, rather, the army of Republika Srpska lines, he led us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had mentioned in your direct evidence that you were part of, let's see, I believe it was the Viteska Brigade, and you used the term, I believe, "date of establishment." What date do you consider as the establishing date of the Viteska Brigade, please?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I know that it came into being towards the end of March 1993, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Karlo Grabovac also your commander in the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was commander of the 3rd Battalion of the Viteska Brigade. As I already said, I was commander of the 2nd Company of the 3rd Battalion in the month of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Grabovac in 1992 have any type of rank? Are you able to recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the superior officer, or to whom was Karlo Grabovac subordinated in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall testifying in the Kupreskic case?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, partly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall being asked that same question by the Prosecution in the Kupreskic case over a year ago about who Karlo Grabovac was subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't recall having had that question put to me, but I know the orders. I know that all the orders that we got to go to the front line against the Serbs I received from Mr. Grabovac and believe me, I wasn't really interested in the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to make sure that we are on the same sheet of music, it was on the 1st of -- I'm sorry, I believe it was the 1st of March, 1999, and the question was asked of you, "Can you tell us who was the commander above you who was authorised to give the orders?" And your answer was, "My commander was Mr. Karlo Grabovac." And you were asked, "And above him, above Mr. Grabovac, who was it?" And your answer was, "I don't know, believe me." When asked about rank, "What was Mr. Grabovac's rank?" Your answer was, "I wouldn't know." How long have you know Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I knew him before the war too. Exactly how many years, that I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to estimate five years, ten years, I mean, you are not that old of a person but as an adult --

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I did not know him as a child, but I knew him as an adult because after all, he's older than I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher please to present two new exhibits, Z765.1 and Z833.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These exhibits will be shown to you, Mr. Rajic, but I have a question before we get to them. Are you able to pinpoint approximately when the HVO was introduced or was founded? Do you know the date?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the events that have been discussed during today's testimony take place subsequent to the founding of the HVO; is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Which events?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The actions in defence of Serb aggression, the Ahmici incident in 1992, all the events that you've talked about today are certainly post-founding; is that correct? They are after April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Everything after April, which is correct, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having -- although you were in a municipal formation, I guess you would call it, during much of 1992, you nonetheless chose to subordinate yourself to the Croat command as opposed to the existing regular TO command; is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It is correct that I did accede to the Croat Defence Council because Croat Defence Council was the first to go to defend the front line against the aggression of the army of Republika Srpska whereas the TO did not do that at the outset. They did do it later though. They went in the direction of Sarajevo to defend that area Visoko, Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There has been previously admitted an exhibit which again we will not ask to be reshown, but it is a list from Z70.2 which discusses a membership in the HDZ from 1991 to 1992. I will simply ask the usher, if possible, because those do not -- it would be on page 66, the fourth line from the top. If you could take a look. Do you see the number four entry? Are you able to see okay?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This list is previously introduced before this Court into evidence and your name appears as Zdenko (Franjo) son of Franjo Rajic, with your date of birth, from Rijeka. Is that your signature at the edge of the page over in the right-hand column?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Looking back at the two documents that I've just asked the usher to put down, Z765.1 is a document dated 21st of April, 1993, and it is signed by Mario Cerkez. Point number four in the order indicates that he is appointing Karlo Grabovac as the commander of the 4th Kruscica Sector which encompasses your area of Rijeka. Have you ever seen this order before?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cerkez was the commander of Mr. Grabovac even in 1992, was he not?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know, but this is what the document says and that could be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, of course, is from 1993, but I'm asking you if you recall Mr. Cerkez being the commander of Mr. Grabovac in 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I personally know that Mr. Mario Cerkez worked on our assignments as to who would be deployed at the front line against the Serbs, but who carried out this particular duty, that I don't know, because he, himself, went with us a few times to the lines up there against the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he go with you and Mr. Grabovac and other members of your battalion and company?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: There weren't any battalions or companies at the time, but they did go with us. In 1992, there weren't any battalions and companies though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the leader of the group, however to wish to describe their military formation? Was there anyone more authoritative than Mr. Cerkez at that time? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I did not really understand you. What do you mean who had more, Grabovac or Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, let's look at it that way. Was it Grabovac or Cerkez who had more at the time, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I know of one action -- well, it wasn't really an action. People were going up to the front line against the army of Republika Srpska, and Mr. Mario Cerkez went with us. At that moment, Grabovac did not go with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was everyone else who typically went on these missions from your local group of soldiers, however you wish to describe their formation? Were they all from the Rijeka area?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: These who went with me, well, in this group, there were about 20 of us. These were locals were Rijeka and in part from Kruscica, but most were from Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mario Cerkez was from where?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: From Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he come in and join you or was he in -- did he start off in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the same location you all started out from? If you went out in the morning was he with you from the beginning or did he join you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: All were volunteers. He joined us immediately from the place that we had set out from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is Z833.1, if you would have a look at it, please. This document is dated 27 April 1993, and it is for the sector commanders and is signed by Mario Cerkez as the commander of the Vitez Brigade. There is a specific order in this to Karlo Grabovac in point number 4. Were you part of the group under Mr. Grabovac which implemented this order?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: At that time, I was at the front line up at Crveno Brdce, feature 517.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us an idea of -- excuse me. Let me just check this for a second. On the morning of the 16th of April, 1992, can you give us an idea, please, of how you heard ultimately about the Ahmici events, the incident at Ahmici? By what means did you learn it if you weren't there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
