utterances.text: At the end of 1992, in your assessment, would the quality of communications in the two places have been broadly similar?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't answer that because I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in Vitez at the end of 1992 -- Your Honour I'm referring to the evidence from Brule and Mr. Koenig who spoke specifically about Gornji Vakuf. Did you, by the end of 1992, through the HVO, have control of the local telephone network?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: It wasn't HVO's control. It was simply the civilian structure which we simply kept such a system, the switchboard in Vitez, but HVO did not control that exchange or the links. It was still under the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There's one other document I want to you look at. It probably won't be necessary to become an exhibit. It can be if necessary. It's 176.1. If becomes an exhibit, let's reserve the position and show the original to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is just simply to, again, confirm the steps that you were taking. This is a receipt for expenditure on repair of telecommunication systems as early as August of 1992. If you can have a quick look at it. Do you remember putting things in order as early as August of 1992 and spending I think some 500-odd Deutschemarks on some pieces of repair?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, at the Technical Overhaul Repair Institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. I needn't put that in as an exhibit, Your Honour, it's enough to remind the witness of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So careful steps were being taken from the beginning to get the equipment in good order, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we were trying to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here's another reflection of that, it's still in 1992, Exhibit 287.2 where we see no lesser a person than Petkovic himself giving out instructions about packet communications which you've helpfully explained to us, and he was explaining that -- just about half way down the screen -- staff commanders will designate a separate room for working with packet communications and select persons and so on. So that there were instructions from the top level about packet communications well before the end of 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: There was no need for such a document to be from General Petkovic because such a document could have been issued by Commander Blaskic, because this is addressed to the HVO command, that is, to the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it all reveals the proper priority, at least the priority being given to an efficient communication system, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, radio packets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed if we look at 2.5 in your own summary of evidence, Mr. Blaz, we find that overall you don't suggest the systems weren't working. You put it like this, and I'm going to quote you from your own summary, "We managed to establish a communication system. It had a lot of weak points so periodically it happened that communications didn't work due to complete or partial malfunctioning of the system. And after the conflict, this became more noticeable." That's as far as you know, isn't it? You had a proper communication system that periodically didn't work.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Well, if you think that's a proper communications system, then that's your view. But I think that that is a communications system who barely met the minimum requirements bearing in mind that there was a whole range of technical breakdowns that we might possibly have, and also major problems when training people to cope with that. I think that this communication system barely met the minimal requirements of communication and in view of what I have just said, you can well imagine how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm only quoting to you from your own summary, but you help us with this then, please. Can you point us to any instance where a failure of an ability to communicate harmed the HVO's interests? Can you point to any order that wasn't given when it should have been or to any order that should have been countermanded or cancelled and that wasn't countermanded or cancelled? Can you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I cannot do that because I am a person who could not even see those documents. And if a document had not passed through, then it did not pass through for technical reasons, but I could not see the document to make any estimates of my own. I simply could not do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You can't tell us either of any instance when Blaskic came to you and said, "As a result of your rotten communications system, we were unable to communicate with X or we were unable to compel this unit to go somewhere else." You don't point to any such instance, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Well, he was a flexible person and a person who knew what it was and appreciated the effort. And he also knew that we were simply powerless and that, therefore, there was no need for him to use such vocabulary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm going to just press you to give you one more chance. Forget the vocabulary and please point us, if you can, to any instance when you say shortcomings of the communication system was a problem because Blaskic identified it to you as a problem. Give us one instance, please.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I could quote a number of such examples, but I do not know what documents it was about and whether these documents were of major value, because all sorts of information and documents went through. But I can show exactly that the shortcomings of the packet system or any other system could result in the fact that we wouldn't be able to issue an order or send a document. There were quite a number of examples when we were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. unable to put things in order and make them work again. But when it would happen, when, for instance, we would be lacking a communication system over a longer period of time, he was a person who could understood why that was. And he could not but realise what we had to face up to, because we did not have adequate technical means and why we were not always able to meet all our obligations, if some order of his had to pass through or any other document and the equipment did not work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only a few more documents. But as we are coming towards the offensive of April 1993, your role was still, was it, as a part-time head of the communications company, commander of the communications company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I think we're talking at cross-purposes. I said, did you ask me about my working hours in 24 hours, or were you asking me about the company which was to provide the communication system in the Operative Zone? I ask you again: Do you mean my working hours, mine as the commander's, or are you asking about the men who were hired to do that, who were doing it; that is, do you mean the whole company or do you mean me only?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you were, in fact, engaged full time on this military work, that's all I want to know, in the first part of 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing on the night of the 15th/16th of April, please?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I was performing some general tasks that I had been made responsible for at the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: At the communications centre in Vitez, in the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Working for Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Well, I worked for the commander of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and that was Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he doing on the night of the 15th/16th of April?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking back, Mr. Blaz, the 15th/16th of April was a pretty important night in the history of Vitez, and an extremely important night in the villages of Ahmici and other neighbouring villages. Now, you must have given some thought at some stage to what was happening that night. Now, will you tell us, please, what was happening?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: You mean after what happened in Ahmici, when the whole front was opened in the Lasva Valley? Are you referring to that day?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm seeking to get from you your memory of what happened on that day, and I'll put to you what happened in due course. You were there, were you, all night, working on the night of the 15th/16th?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Who told you that you were going to be required to work night duty?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Nobody told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you worked night duty on that particular night?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: That was not the only night. Before that, the same thing happened too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure there were other nights when you worked nights, yes. But why did you work nights on this particular night, please?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I worked both that night and a number of other nights, because we had extra large problems with the communications systems. You're expected to maintain those communication lines that flow both ways, upward and downward. It required my presence and the presence of other men in order for this communication to be able to function properly and be there for the command and control purposes. So I don't know why this specific night, because it was just one of the nights when I was there to enable the commander to command and control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if I understand your answer. But first of all, just make sure of this: You're really saying you have no idea why I'm asking you particularly about the night of the 15th/16th of April of 1993; is that your position? You have no idea why I'm asking you about that night.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I don't know why you're asking me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Are you also saying that your night duty on that night was simply because there were problems with the communication system which needed correcting?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly whether we had any specific problems then. But in terms of staying at night in the centre, to sleep over there, that happened frequently. So I believe that there was no particular problem, but I spent the night there as I did many other nights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that your position, therefore, reduces to this, doesn't it: This was a wholly ordinary, unexceptional night and yet one that you can remember, seven years later, as one which you stayed on duty overnight; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know perfectly well that you were on duty that night because there was a major operation, and you as the communications commander were heavily involved in it.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I was unaware of any operations that were about to be carried out, and I was involved in this as I was involved in any plan. There was a monthly plan that I was following on the communication systems. If I stayed one night or two nights or three nights in a month, it would have been for some technical problem or some other reason. The technical problems were not the only reasons why we would stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If a number of units were sent out on Blaskic's order on the night of the 15th/16th and April, or any other night, you had the equipment for those units to stay in contact with base; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, I had nothing to do with such units ever. My task was very loud and clear. It has to do with the communication centre. It was to maintain communication between the command and the subordinate units. What they were involved in, that was not part of what I needed to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I used the word "you" too generally. I'll repeat the question. If a number of units were sent out on Blaskic's order on the night of the 15th/16th of April, or on any other night, the HVO had equipment whereby those units could stay in contact with base; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I cannot say that because I don't know, because I had no units under my own command. I could not follow them. As the commander of the communications centre, I had communication with the communication centres of subordinate units, which would have been brigades. Now, what communication they had in their turn, what they did on their own, that I did not know. It was not my duty to know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that I understand your position. You're able to tell this Court that there were no communications by the politician Kordic, but you're not able to tell this Court anything about communications between soldiers and the communication centre; is that really your position?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I again did not understand you now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I'll try to make it simple. Your position remains, does it, that you can tell this Chamber that there were no communications to your knowledge between the politician Kordic and Blaskic; that remains your position, does it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: My question, again, is what type of communication? I could not forbid Kordic and Blaskic to talk among themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, nevertheless, you're unable to tell us one word about radio or any other form of communications between soldiers or groups of soldiers and Blaskic at the communications centre, you're unable to tell us anything about such communication; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: That is not my position, and I don't know -- could you please repeat the question one more time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if that's not your position, I'll come back to that question. I want to know, please, what radio or other communications happened on the night of the 15th/16th of April of 1993 coming to or going from the communications centre in Vitez where you were?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: At that time, we were using the radio packet communication, which was at the communications centre, and we had the regular radio network going. It was in KV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you also have voice-to-voice communication, ordinary radio communication?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I don't know. What radio communication? UHF, short-wave, or KV? I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm in your hands on this, Mr. Blaz. You've already told us that there was ordinary voice-to-voice communication. Now, I want you to tell us, please, as the communications officer, head of the communications company, what communication was going on on the night that we know ended in Ahmici being massacred? Now, will you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I cannot say anything in that regard. That night and that day, we had regular communication systems; it was operational. We had a network going and a KV system, and all other systems were working. But regardless of whether they were working or not, I wasn't following them, and that was not my task. That was at the level of subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. It's the subordinates to you who would read or hear the messages, and it was your superiors who would be sending them. Is that your account? So that you, as it were, fall in between and you have no knowledge of what was happening.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I didn't need to know whether anything was going on or not going on. The important thing for me was to transmit everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not going to trouble the witness or the Court with any other documents with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Perhaps only a couple of short questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It's more or less because some statements were left in the air, I guess. Re-examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some examples of situations when communications were not working have been mentioned. Is it true that on the 18th of April a shell hit the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the equipment had been damaged at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that some people were injured at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. I was present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this set you back for a period of time in terms of equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the equipment was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the municipal communication centre, OIC, also knocked out of service?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes, for a longer time than we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the communication centre of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that this has not been clarified. You know that on 16 April the general conflict broke out between the two sides in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is how you remember the night between the 15th and the 16th.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that anyone who lives in the Lasva River Valley remembers that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that. That was obviously a leading question and it gets us absolutely no where. The witness has given his answers on his process of recollection, and he doesn't need to be reminded of another method.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise if I was too suggestive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm not sure that it was a particularly controversial matter in the event, but don't lead. Also, bear in mind the time because it's time for a break for the interpreters. If you could wind up, please, Mr. Kovacic, as quick as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will surely be finished in two or three minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the beginning of the cross-examination you were shown two documents that had to do with the procurement of equipment. One was a transponder repeater as it was called, 69/20, and the other one was a model 100 TAM vehicle. Did you see such a piece of equipment, what was called a repeater?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, and I think I said that I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about this command and communication vehicle that was mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, I never saw that either. I don't know that we had it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had such a vehicle, such command communication vehicles appeared in the Lasva Valley, in any of the municipalities of this valley, would you have learned about it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I probably would have, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a professional, would you have been happy to have acquired such a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No doubt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When shown a receipt from the maintenance facility, up to what time were you able to use their services?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Until the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that you had no access there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, we had no access there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also shown a document, the contents of which had to do with the packet communication, it was signed by Petkovic and it was addressed to HVO. Do you recollect that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you glean from the contents of this document that this was -- this had to do with the planning of the system and the acquisition or procurement of the system?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards the end of the cross-examination, you said that radio packet and the KV communication system were both operational on that night between the 15th and the 16th?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the type of communication systems that are used by the command with the local units who were in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, they are absolutely not used for those purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the local level, let's say if your Commander Blaskic wanted to talk to a unit which is some three kilometres from him, would he be using packet communication or KV communication systems?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, he would not use either of the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of communication system would he be using?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: He would use hand-held radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that type of communication would not be physically going through your communication centre?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Not necessarily, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if other units had those mobile hand-held equipment, would you be in charge of the hardware?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is then in charge of the maintenance of this type of equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Services that were part of those units. In other words, their own communication centres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When a transmission comes to you, say, from Kiseljak, it is not your concern how it is transmitted from Kiseljak to the subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: No, that is none of my business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the critical time, and I mean it literally, were you listening in to the communication traffic of the subordinate or superior units?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: I believe that at that time, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have had a reason to listen in in order to just verify that all the systems were working?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BLAZ
utterances.text: Occasionally we can use it, let's say, if we wanted to check on the codes, whether they were being used or not, but that's just a routine check.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you very much. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Blaz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Blaz that concludes your evidence. You are free to go. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal. We will adjourn now until half past 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
